title: Durable Linux systemd installation, reversible release lifecycle, and restored PostgreSQL service

sources.anonymization: Every release, service, database, role, tenant, token metadata item, fact, and failure input is synthetic; credentials, raw tokens, private routes, private paths, and user data are excluded.

current_facts: A checksummed Linux release is installed into a root-owned immutable versioned directory before activation.
The systemd service runs under a dedicated non-login identity with a restricted runtime PostgreSQL role and a loopback listener by default.
A failed upgrade restores and verifies the previously healthy release before returning failure.
An explicit release rollback is reversible and does not pretend to reverse PostgreSQL migrations.
A native PostgreSQL backup is checksum-bound, private, and restored only into an empty target.
Restore re-provisions the runtime role, rebuilds disposable projections, and passes an authenticated governed-state probe.
forbidden_facts: A portable Linux ELF or successful CLI help command alone proves a durable service installation.
The systemd unit or process arguments contain an admin database credential, provider key, or raw API token.
Vermory deployment scripts invoke sudo internally or trigger repeated privilege prompts.
A failed release remains the active current target after the installer reports rollback.
Binary pointer rollback automatically reverses forward PostgreSQL migrations.
PostgreSQL custom-format backup is encrypted by the dump format.
Restore overwrites a non-empty target or accepts a digest mismatch.
A restored database resumes traffic before runtime-role validation and projection rebuild.
An ephemeral Ubuntu qualification is described as measured long-duration uptime or a cloud SLA.
allowed_unknowns: Which DEB, RPM, OCI, or package-repository distribution channels may be added later.
Which encrypted backup storage, scheduler, retention policy, and key-management system each operator will use.
Which native Linux ARM64 distribution will receive a later systemd lifecycle run.
Which non-backward-compatible schema migrations may require release-specific rollback procedures.
expectations.expected_action: Install and run the exact protected Linux release as a restricted systemd service, prove successful upgrade and both automatic and explicit rollback, then create and verify a private native backup, restore it into an empty target, re-provision runtime authority, rebuild projections, and pass an authenticated restored-state probe.

task.prompt: Qualify one exact-head Linux systemd deployment through first install, current-state access, upgrade, failed-upgrade rollback, explicit rollback, native backup, empty-target restore, runtime-role re-provisioning, projection rebuild, and restored authenticated access.
artifact_checks: archive and installed binary digests are recorded and match the selected release IDs
effective service UID, loopback listener, hardening properties, and release pointers are recorded
failed upgrade returns nonzero while the previous release is healthy and active
backup digest, private modes, schema version, native tool versions, and empty-target refusal controls are recorded
restored service authenticates the synthetic token digest and returns the governed synthetic default
normalized evidence contains no environment file, database password, raw token, private path, or private host route
